- When sentiment turns sharply negative or news volume spikes, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a strong upward spike in sentiment, model often fails to mean-revert; apply a 3–5 day lagged mean reversion correction.
- If sentiment is consistently low or flat over 5+ days, model overestimates downward trend — adjust forecast downward by 2–5%.
- Model underestimates true price when sentiment is high and news volume is low — increase forecast by 3–7% if sentiment > 0.67 and news < 2.0.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts in high-news environments — apply 1–3% downward bias if news volume > 3.0.
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is high, model often fails to adjust quickly — apply 2–4% downward correction to avoid overcorrection lag.
